claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,n), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x: the Pollard-rho algorithm with distinguished points and the full secp256k1 automorphism group (order 6) in proof.md succeeds with probability at least 0.49 using at most 2^128.84065 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, automorphism reduction, table operations and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^95 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^15 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. Heuristics used: standard Pollard-rho random-walk model on the automorphism quotient (supported by the Teske / van Oorschot-Wiener / Bos et al. literature), negligible fruitless-cycle impact with r=32 partitions, and overwhelming probability that collision coefficients are usable. This is an analytic cryptanalytic claim under exploratory review, not a practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Check Pollard-rho scalar recovery (with negation-map orbit reduction) on a small additive cyclic group. This does not establish production curve behavior, automorphism costs, memory bounds, or operation costs.

title: secp256k1-ecdlp: Pollard rho with order-6 automorphisms
